notes: §1985:VIII.4.2.4 GR2 puts a relative file in the non-sequential category: CLOSE is A (implementor closing operations, labels by the implementor's convention) and CLOSE WITH LOCK is A,B, "The file is locked and cannot be opened again during this execution of this run unit" (a later OPEN is status 38, §1985:VIII.1.3.4). SequentialIoBinder#BindClose refuses REEL/UNIT/NO REWIND on a non-sequential file (COBOL1693; the 1985 relative format has only WITH LOCK); FileRegistry#CloseByFormat executes the non-unit cell (close file, 42 when not open), and FileRegistry#CloseWithLock locks only after a successful close. Probes at 85: random and dynamic access, LABEL RECORDS STANDARD and OMITTED; CLOSE and CLOSE WITH LOCK of an unopened file -> 42 and the file then opens 00; after WITH LOCK, OPEN INPUT, I-O and OUTPUT each -> 38 with USE run; CLOSE of the locked file -> 42; the lock survives CANCEL and re-CALL of the locking subprogram (38); CLOSE REEL, UNIT FOR REMOVAL, NO REWIND refused, bare CLOSE refused. The witness writes, reads, closes, closes WITH LOCK and gets 38 in the USE procedure. The refuter's DIVERGES (refute-rd-05/c3b.cob: an OPEN of the same physical file through another file-name answered 00 and read) is fixed by kb/Work PB5210: at --std 85 the lock is the physical file's (PhysicalFileTable.State.ClosedWithLock, asked by FileRegistry#ClosedWithLock in SharedOpenAttempt), so no file-name of any program reopens it in the run unit; witness pb5210_close_lock_locks_physical_file_85 (all three organizations).

File Lock The file is locked and cannot be opened again during this execution of this run unit."; 2023: "| CLOSE | c | c,f | a,c,f | c | ... c) Close file Closing operations specified by the implementor are executed.". 2023 keeps the non-sequential category and plain CLOSE (implementor closing operations) but has no CLOSE WITH LOCK row (file lock B) and no label-record processing.
